filename: The Modèle Atmosphérique Régional–Intelligence Artificielle (MAR-IA)_ surface meltwater over Greenland._
title: The Modèle Atmosphérique Régional – Intelligence Artificielle (MAR-IA): surface meltwater over Greenland
code_availability: The MAR-IA models and the training datasets can be found here - https://zenodo.org/records/17942115.
testbed_rationale: Provides a clean, publicly archived benchmark dataset on Zenodo (1979–2024 daily surface energy balance components and meltwater production across Greenland) designed specifically for training and evaluating machine learning emulators.
pain_points: Multicollinearity among surface energy balance predictors (e.g., surface/skin temperature and 2 m air temperature) which obscures feature attribution.
Physical saturation effects (skin temperature saturating at 0 °C during melt periods, or albedo saturating at low values during prolonged ablation), limiting predictor sensitivity.
Poor representation / lack of spatial variability of albedo in global reanalysis datasets (ERA5) severely degrading emulator performance when MAR albedo is unavailable.
High computational overhead of SHAP (Shapley value) feature attribution over large spatiotemporal datasets, necessitating subsampling.
extraction_notes: The paper acknowledges funding from the NSF LEAP STC (Award number 2019625). While evaluations are shown for K-transect S6 and Swiss Camp locations, comparisons are made between the emulator and MAR model outputs at the grid points corresponding to those stations rather than direct assimilation of in-situ AWS measurements.
